title: HamonSequence
description: Canonical JSON representation of a hamon harmony sequence. This is the hub of the hamon standard: all source formats (MEI, MusicXML, Humdrum, LilyPond, ABC, MuseScore) map to and from this structure. The text surface syntax (grammar/hamon.ebnf) is the serialization of this JSON into a compact string form. Version 0.2.0 adds the optional analytical layer (tonal regions, tonicizations, secondary dominants, layered functional analysis, non-harmonic-tone melodic analysis, modal harmony, omitted fundamentals, arpeggiation, and alternative whole-progression analyses); see documentation/analysis.md. Version 0.2.1 adds the optional HarmonyGroup.position (time-aligned position from positioned formats such as MEI @tstamp/@startid). Version 0.4.0 adds the optional top-level meters array (time signatures, surface '@meter:N/D') that bounds the valid Position.beat range. Version 0.5.0 adds Position.seconds (surface 's:12.34'), the physical-time clock, so that audio-time sources (Harte .lab, JAMS) keep the only position they state; the clocks coexist and none is derived from another. All analytical and positional fields are optional and backward compatible with 0.1.0 documents.

HamonSequence.description: A complete harmony sequence, optionally scoped to a notation system.

version.description: The HAMON standard version this sequence targets, as a semver string (e.g. '0.1.0'). Maps to the @version:<semver> surface directive. Absent means version is unspecified.

sequenceSystemHint.description: Optional declaration of the notation system for the whole sequence (@cs, @rn, @ns, @fb, @fun, @text, @auto). When absent, each label's system is detected individually.

groups.description: Ordered list of harmony groups, one per time point (beat, measure, or event).

meters.description: Optional time signatures (v0.4.0): the meter in effect, declared at the start and at every metric change. Each meter's numerator is the beat count and thus bounds the valid range of a group's Position.beat (MEI data.BEAT): beat spans [1, numerator+1). Surface: '@meter:N/D' directive lines. A beat outside its meter is a non-blocking warning. See documentation/positions.md.

regions.description: Optional analytical layer (v0.2.0): tonal regions, modulations and tonicizations spanning ranges of groups. Each region declares the local key in force over [fromGroup, toGroup]. Surface: '@key:' directive lines and ':' / 'of' tonicization spans. See documentation/analysis.md.

alternativeAnalyses.description: Optional analytical layer (v0.2.0): alternative whole-progression readings of (a span of) the same sequence — e.g. two analysts proposing different Roman-numeral progressions, or a chord-symbol reading vs. a functional reading. For single-time-point alternatives use HarmonyGroup.alternatives instead.

HarmonyGroup.description: The harmony at one time point. Primary labels are the main reading; alternatives are other simultaneous interpretations (e.g., two analysts' readings, or layered encodings).

primary.description: The primary harmony labels at this time point. Most sequences have exactly one primary label per group.

alternatives.description: Alternative simultaneous readings. Each element is a list of labels forming one alternative layer.

position.description: Optional time-aligned position of this group in the source (v0.2.1). Populated when imported from a positioned format (e.g. MEI @tstamp / @startid); absent for line-ordered surfaces, where group order is the only positional information.

Meter.description: A time signature (v0.4.0) declared with the '@meter:N/D' surface directive, at the start and at every metric change. numerator is the beat count and bounds the valid range of a group's Position.beat (MEI data.BEAT): beat spans [1, numerator+1). fromGroup is the index of the first group it governs.

numerator.description: Beats per measure (the time-signature numerator); bounds the valid Position.beat range.

fromGroup.description: Index into groups of the first group this meter governs (until the next meter).

Fraction.description: An exact rational number (e.g. a metric position in quarter notes).

Position.description: A time-aligned position for a HarmonyGroup (v0.2.1). All fields optional: measure+beat mirror an MEI @tstamp; time is an absolute musical offset; seconds is physical time (v0.5); ref points at a score-object id (MEI @startid). A position carries whichever of these the source provided, and none is derived from another.

beat.description: Beat within the measure (1-based; may be fractional, mirroring MEI @tstamp).

time.description: Absolute fractional position from the start, in QUARTER notes — the unit every source HAMON reads uses (DCML quarterbeats, Dezrann start, DiLeMMa, music21 offsets).

seconds.description: Absolute PHYSICAL time from the start, in seconds (v0.5) — audio or a performance (Harte .lab, JAMS). A different clock from `time`: it is stored only when the source stated it, and is never converted to or from musical time.

ref.description: Reference to a score-object id the harmony is anchored to (e.g. MEI @startid).

HarmonyLabel.description: A single harmony label: the exact surface string plus its normalized semantic and rendering hints.

surface.description: The exact original string as it appeared in the source (glyphs preserved). This is the lossless representation.

sequenceSystemHint.description: System hint declared at sequence level, propagated here for convenience.

detectedSystem.description: The notation system as detected by the grammar from the surface form.

system.description: The resolved notation system: equals detectedSystem unless a sequenceSystemHint overrides it.

semantic.description: Normalized semantic content. May be absent for unparsed or deferred labels.

rendering.description: The glyphs the source used for accidentals, quality, and seventh — needed to round-trip back to the original surface.

layer.description: Optional analytical layer (v0.2.0). When several labels in one HarmonyGroup describe the SAME sonority from different analytical viewpoints (a vertical 'analysis stack'), each carries a distinct layer tag: e.g. a 'degree' Roman numeral, a 'function' T/S/D token, a 'chord' chord-symbol, a 'bass' figured-bass, and a 'key' label, all aligned at one time point. Absent for a plain single-reading label.

localKey.description: Optional analytical layer (v0.2.0). The local key in force for this label, when it differs from the prevailing region (e.g. inside a tonicization). For Roman numerals this is the key the degree is measured against.

attributes.description: Optional analytical layer (v0.2.0): analytical attributes of this harmony (omitted fundamental, rootless voicing, inversion, arpeggiation/prolongation, tonicization target, secondary-dominant application, pedal).

HarmonySemantic.description: The normalized semantic content of a harmony label. Discriminated by the 'kind' field.

ChordSymbolSemantic.description: A chord symbol (American/jazz notation): root pitch, triad quality, optional seventh, extensions, alterations, and slash bass.

root.description: The root pitch of the chord.

bass.description: Slash bass note (e.g., C/E). Absent when there is no inversion or pedal point.

quality.description: The triad quality. Defaults to 'major' when no quality marker is written.

seventh.description: The seventh interval, if present. Absent for triads.

extensions.description: Added tension intervals beyond the seventh (9, 11, 13).

adds.description: Added tones (add9, add11) that do not imply lower extensions.

suspensions.description: Suspended intervals (sus, sus2, sus4). Null means 'sus' without a specific interval.

RomanSemantic.description: A Roman numeral label (scale-degree analysis). Case encodes mode: uppercase = major, lowercase = minor.

degree.description: The Roman numeral degree as written (e.g., 'V', 'iv', 'II'). Case is preserved.

prefixAccidentals.description: Accidental glyphs preceding the degree (e.g., ['b'] for bVII, ['#'] for #IV). Surface glyphs are preserved.

secondary.description: Secondary function target written after '/' (e.g., 'V' in V/V). Roman token only, without accidentals.

tail.description: Remaining surface after the degree: figures, quality suffixes, etc. (e.g., '65', '°7', 'b5'). Not further parsed at this level.

NashvilleSemantic.description: A Nashville number system label (scale-degree chord symbol using integers).

prefixAccidentals.description: Accidental glyphs preceding the number (e.g., ['b'] for b7).

tail.description: Quality and extension suffix after the number (e.g., 'm', 'maj7', 'sus4').

secondary.description: Secondary target after '/' (e.g., '5' in 1/5, or a pitch name).

FiguredBassSemantic.description: A figured bass label (interval figures above a bass note, Baroque continuo notation).

prefixAccidentals.description: Accidental glyphs preceding the primary figure.

tail.description: Remaining figures written after the primary one (e.g., '-5' in '6-5', '-3' in '4-3').

FunctionalSemantic.description: A Riemannian functional harmony label (T, S, D and their variants, optionally chained with '->').

chain.description: The sequence of functional tokens. Single-element for a plain label; multiple elements for a progression chain (e.g., ['D', 'T'] for D->T).

NoChordSemantic.description: Explicit absence of harmony (no chord symbol, rest, or tacet).

TextSemantic.description: A lossless fallback for labels that could not be parsed into any other semantic kind. The original text is preserved verbatim.

text.description: The raw label text, exactly as it appeared in the source.

ToneSemantic.description: Analytical layer (v0.2.0): a single melodic note classified for harmonic/non-harmonic analysis. Used on a 'melodic' analytical layer to annotate chord tones (HT) and non-chord tones (NHT: passing, neighbor, suspension, appoggiatura, etc.). The Fuxian changing-note / nota cambiata is encoded as type 'cambiata'.

pitch.description: The sounding pitch class of the note, when known.

category.description: Whether the tone belongs to the prevailing harmony (harmonic / HT) or not (nonharmonic / NHT).

type.description: The kind of non-harmonic tone. Required when category = 'nonharmonic'; absent (or 'chord-tone') when harmonic.

metric.description: Metric placement, distinguishing e.g. accented vs. unaccented passing tones and appoggiatura vs. unaccented neighbor.

approach.description: Melodic motion into the tone (how it is approached from the previous note).

departure.description: Melodic motion out of the tone (how it resolves to the next note).

voice.description: Optional voice/part identifier the tone belongs to (e.g. 'soprano', 'bass', 'v1').

NonHarmonicType.description: Classification of a non-harmonic (non-chord) tone. 'cambiata' covers the Fuxian nota cambiata / changing-note figure; 'pedal' is a sustained pedal/organ point.

Motion.description: Melodic motion direction/manner used to characterize how a tone is approached or left.

Mode.description: Tonality/mode of a key. Supports common-practice major/minor and the diatonic church modes for modal-harmony analysis. 'major' is an alias of 'ionian' and 'minor' of 'aeolian'; both spellings are allowed so sources can preserve their own vocabulary.

Key.description: Analytical layer (v0.2.0): a tonal centre — a tonic pitch class plus a mode. Used for tonal regions, local keys of tonicizations, and modal-harmony contexts.

tonic.description: The tonic pitch class of the key (e.g. C, F#, Bb).

mode.description: The mode/tonality. Defaults to 'major' when absent.

label.description: Optional human-readable key label as written in the source (e.g. 'C', 'a', 'D dorian', 'Bb:').

TonalRegion.description: Analytical layer (v0.2.0): a span of groups governed by one local key. 'kind' distinguishes a stable home/region key, a passing tonicization (brief secondary-dominant target), and a confirmed modulation. Regions may nest (a tonicization inside a region) via 'parent'.

key.description: The local key in force over this span.

kind.description: 'key'/'region' = a tonal area; 'tonicization' = a brief emphasis of a degree as a local tonic (regiones tonales pasajeras); 'modulation' = a confirmed change of key.

fromGroup.description: Index (into HamonSequence.groups) of the first group in this span, inclusive.

toGroup.description: Index of the last group in this span, inclusive. Absent means the region runs until the next region of the same level or the end of the sequence.

degree.description: For tonicizations/regions expressed relative to a parent key: the scale degree being tonicized (e.g. 'V', 'ii', 'bVI'), i.e. the target of a secondary function.

parent.description: Index into HamonSequence.regions of the enclosing region, when this region is nested (e.g. a V/V tonicization inside the dominant region).

label.description: Optional source label for the region (e.g. 'V of V', 'C: ... :', 'mediant region').

scales.description: Chord-scale(s) valid over this region (jazz/Berklee), from the '@scale:' directive. Per-chord scales live on HarmonyAttributes.scales.

AnalyticalLayer.description: The analytical viewpoint a label expresses within a HarmonyGroup's vertical analysis stack. Enables multi-layer functional analysis: a melodic/bass layer, a tonality layer, a tonal-function layer, and a scale-degree layer can coexist at one time point.

HarmonyAttributes.description: Analytical layer (v0.2.0): optional analytical attributes attached to a HarmonyLabel. All properties are optional.

inversion.description: Inversion: 0 = root position, 1 = first inversion, 2 = second, 3 = third.

omittedRoot.description: Fundamental omitida: the chord's root/fundamental is not sounded but is analytically understood (e.g. an incomplete dominant seventh, or a rootless jazz voicing analysed with its implied root).

rootless.description: The voicing omits the root by performance convention (jazz rootless voicing). Distinct from 'omittedRoot', which is an analytical claim about an implied fundamental.

impliedRoot.description: The understood fundamental when it is omitted from the sounding chord.

arpeggiated.description: Despliegue: the chord is realized as an arpeggio/broken chord unfolding over time rather than sounded as a block.

prolongation.description: How this harmony prolongs/elaborates a structural harmony (Schenkerian-style): an arpeggiation, a pedal, a neighbor or passing chord, or a general prolongation.

prolongs.description: Index (into HamonSequence.groups) of the structural harmony that this label prolongs/elaborates.

pedal.description: The harmony sounds over a pedal point (sustained bass).

tonicizes.description: The scale degree this harmony tonicizes (e.g. 'V' for a chord that tonicizes the dominant). Pairs with secondary-dominant Roman numerals like V/V.

applied.description: Secondary/applied function (secondary dominant, dominant of the dominant, applied leading-tone chord). The target is the degree the applied chord resolves to.

target.description: The degree the applied chord resolves to, e.g. 'V' in V7/V, 'ii' in V/ii.

chain.description: Nested application chain for stacked secondaries (e.g. ['V','V'] for V/V/V), outermost first.

scales.description: Chord-scale(s) valid over this chord (jazz/Berklee), from one or more '[scale:NAME]' attributes (e.g. G7 → altered / lydian-dominant).

duration.description: Extent (v0.4.1), surface '[dur:3/4]': how long this reading lasts, in QUARTER notes — the same unit as Position.time. It sits on the LABEL, not the group, so two alternative readings can segment the same passage differently. Set ONLY from what a source stated (Dezrann 'duration', DCML 'duration_qb', AugmentedNet 'a_duration', MEI @tstamp2). Absent means unknown: the rule that a harmony runs to the next group is a computation, and is never stored as if it were data.

durationSeconds.description: Extent (v0.5), surface '[dur:1.85s]': how long this reading lasts in SECONDS — the same clock as Position.seconds. The extent inherits the clock of the source that stated it, so '[dur:…]' is one key with an optional 's' suffix: bare is quarter notes (see duration), suffixed is physical time (Harte's start/end, JAMS 'duration'). Never derived from duration or the reverse — crossing the clocks needs a tempo map the label stream does not have.

endRef.description: Extent (v0.4.1), surface '[endref:note-12]': the score object this harmony ends on (MEI @endid), the structural counterpart of Position.ref. Use when the source anchors to objects rather than to time.

ScaleSpec.description: A chord-scale (jazz/Berklee): the recommended scale for a chord or region. 'name' is an open vocabulary (church modes plus altered, lydian-dominant, locrian-natural-2, whole-tone, diminished-hw/-wh, harmonic-minor, melodic-minor, bebop-dominant, blues, …).

tonic.description: The scale's tonic when it differs from the implied one (the chord root / region key).

pitches.description: Explicit pitch classes of the scale, for non-standard scales.

AlternativeAnalysis.description: Analytical layer (v0.2.0): one alternative whole-progression reading of a span of the sequence. Lets multiple analyses of the same music coexist (different analysts, or a chord-symbol vs. Roman-numeral vs. functional reading).

label.description: Identifier for this alternative reading (e.g. analyst name, source, or 'functional').

system.description: The notation system this alternative reading is expressed in, when uniform.

scope.description: The span of the primary sequence this alternative re-analyses. Absent = the whole sequence.

groups.description: The alternative reading itself, as a full list of harmony groups covering 'scope'.

PitchClass.description: A pitch class: a note letter (A–G) with an optional accidental. Enharmonic spelling is preserved from the source.

accidental.description: The accidental, if any. Absent means natural (no accidental written).

Accidental.description: A normalized accidental token. The surface glyph (e.g., '#', '♯', 'b', '♭') that produced this value is stored in RenderingHints.accidentalGlyphs.

ChordQuality.description: The triad quality of a chord symbol.

SeventhQuality.description: The seventh interval quality. 'dom7' = minor seventh above a major triad (C7). 'maj7' = major seventh (Cmaj7). 'min7' = minor seventh above a minor triad (Cm7). 'dim7' = diminished seventh (C°7). 'hdim7' = minor seventh above a diminished triad (Cø7).

glyph.description: The exact accidental glyph used in the source (e.g., '#', '♯', 'b', '♭').

RenderingHints.description: The surface glyphs used in the original label, needed to reconstruct the original string losslessly. These are display preferences, not semantic content.

accidentalGlyphs.description: Map from normalized accidental to the glyph written in the source (e.g., {"sharp": "♯"} or {"flat": "b"}).

rawParts.description: Fragments of the surface that were not interpreted into any semantic field but must be preserved for lossless round-trip.

SequenceSystem.description: A notation system hint for a whole sequence, as declared by a '@<id>' prefix line.

DetectedSystem.description: The notation system as resolved for a specific label (detected by the grammar, optionally overridden by a SequenceSystem hint).
